## Validated contributions on 2026-11-15

1. **Escaped source-map JSON disclosure preflight:** The prior `src/source-maps.js` string-prefix filter could miss valid version-three map objects whose JSON keys use Unicode escapes (e.g. `"ver\\u0073ion"`). Replaced with a cheap object-shaped check plus structural inspection of parsed JSON keys. Added `test/source-map-json-escapes.test.js` for escaped-key and indexed-map canaries, strings, Buffers, BOM/whitespace, COO/SCO/SNO and programmatic SCO publication; ordinary JSON and binary assets remain accepted. Added test to manual semantics workflow. Green Linux/Windows run 43709319407 at SHA `6aee06b52ed9e2eb3eb2f42132b5c3a7b651a473`. Report: `im-results/escaped-source-map-keys-2026-11-15.md`. This is build-time accidental disclosure prevention only, no client anti-extraction guarantee.

2. **Immutable local identity wrappers:** Extended `src/properties.js` `proveLocalObject` to track `const f=x=>x`, block arrow return, and `const f=function(x){return x;}` (including named expression), with plain params and a simple returned parameter. Existing lexical, source-observer, call-site, escape and ambiguity checks remain. `test/local-identity-wrapper.test.js` runs 6 accepted and 7 declined/counterexample cases in COO/SNO against native runtime; cross-file property flow not modified. It now runs the offline source-only `sims/offline-normalize.js` attacker: both generated private-key labels per accepted fixture are removed with identical fixture behavior. Test integrated into `manual-transform-safety.yml`. Green Linux/Windows run 43709847473 at `33e533f91761f07957e54cf083290013952b465c`. Report: `im-results/local-identity-flow-2026-11-15.md`.

3. **SNO hot path evidence:** Added two million-iteration identity-wrapper workloads to `sims/hotpath-mixed.js`; each asserted 2 renamed private fields. Green Ubuntu run 43709949069 at `100096a728d4197f4260b716514051e914f4e729` (Node 22, warm-up 8, alternating 15 trials). Arrow original 1.414788 ms, transformed 1.431309 ms, ratio 1.01167737×. Function-expression original 1.420208 ms, transformed 1.451176 ms, ratio 1.02180526×. These pass 2.5× *for this warmed SNO sample*; cold COO and arbitrary workload budgets remain unverified. Static normalizer undoes the syntactic key layer, so no meaningful reconstruction resistance demonstrated.

## Research integrity

All scores here describe finite tests. The adversary has complete client code/runtime in COO, owner code/runtime/files in SNO, and unlimited legitimate RPC requests in SCO. Locally protected labels are mechanically removed; server-private SCO remains vulnerable to chosen-input functional cloning and small work RPC latency. Never promote a test count or “green CI” to proof of tamper resistance, authorized-execution enforcement or general 2.5× compliance.

## Second verified contribution: SCO immutable async expression partition

- Extended `src/sco-partition.js` from only exported direct `async function` declarations to `export const f=async (...)=>...` and `export const f=async function name(...) {...}` with only identifier parameters. Proxy expression exports are emitted as async function expressions, preserving metadata `.name`, `.length`, nonconstructibility and `[...arguments]` actual length, including omitted/extra positional args. Opaque/mutable, sync, generator, default/rest/destructured params and `this`/`super` users still refused. `serverOnlyInitialization:true` retains trusted private module imports and closed-over secrets. Authenticated request and method authorization remain caller-defined. Updated `docs/SCO_PARTITION.md`.
- New `test/sco-partition-const-functions.test.js` imports actual ESM originals, serves private canary-free proxies over real HTTP, executes client from child Node process, compares normal + omitted/extra JSON args, tests `.name`/`.length`, batch, unauthorized request, invalid exports. Included in `.github/workflows/manual-sco-authorization.yml`. First workflow run showed only an obsolete message regex in legacy private-init test; updated `test/sco-partition-private-init.test.js`. Green Windows/Linux focused SCO + JSDoc run 43710796219 exact SHA `29dfb944adcc64ab571b17de2f17f46936955e21`. Full repository validation (behavior, attacks, benchmarks, JSDoc, Chromium on Ubuntu) green run 43710935370 exact SHA `2c9fa1465149f8c11fa5f115e4bfff06eaf68a07`.
- New `sims/sco-const-granularity.js` paired direct original and genuine authenticated loopback generated-client RPC. Two after-warmup 12-sample experiments per OS: 1-iteration tiny direct vs RPC **321.64× Linux**, **294.89× Windows**, fails 2.5×; 6,000,000-iteration coarse **1.16557× Linux** and **1.15380× Windows**, within 2.5× for this sample. Deterministic 254-byte original source and 617-byte served source across OS, private canary absent from served. Green SCO CI run 43711333317 exact SHA `101ab12b475d2b1e2063eb971c54dd4c6e878809`. Report: `im-results/sco-immutable-async-partition-2026-11-15.md`. No claim for WAN, cold client init or universal steady-state overhead.
- Sent mailbox messages to agent5 (SCO partition), agent7 (property analysis), agent25 (asset disclosure) with pinned evidence and safety limits. These are under `communications/agent5`, `communications/agent7`, and `communications/agent25`, dated 2026-11-15T1152Z.

- `test/cross-file-local-identity.test.js` is independent held-out ESM corpus: 7 graph kinds × 3 deterministic seeds = 21 three-module cases. Native Node ESM runner installs an untracked `globalThis.window.api` host before dynamic import. 9 positive graphs contain imported private object forwarded through immutable local arrow, function expression, block arrow, const/let aliases; private keys 2 each renamed (18 positive key instances). 12 negative graphs refuse due untracked window API reflection/argument escape, dynamic host key, observing wrapper or callback escape. They show safe renaming of selected private shape, while the static attacker still neutralizes recognizable hash labels. Avoid conflating graph counts with full JS semantics or attack resilience.

## Fourth verified contribution: local private zero-argument getters

- Expanded `src/properties.js` closed-world proof with `returnsRoot?:boolean` for pure synchronous zero-argument getter returning exactly a candidate owner lexically: `const f=()=>root`, `const f=()=>{return root;}`, `const f=function local(){return root;}` and `function f(){return root;}`. The returned owner is admitted only through tracked alias capture or discarded expression. Unknown consumption `get().secret`, getter escape or export, callback use, async, parameterized/effectful getters and reflection decline. `test/local-root-getter.test.js` compares four admitted/8 declined cases against native COO/SNO and static source-only normalization plus 2 exported module declines.
- Extended independent `test/cross-file-local-identity.test.js` to **11 graph kinds ×3 seeds=33 three-module Node ESM graphs** using a real untracked `globalThis.window.api` external object. 15 positive (5 forms×3) rename 2 eligible keys each = **30/30 private-key occurrences**, and 18 refusal (6 forms×3) rename 0. All baseline, transformed and attacker-normalized results match. The static attacker still strips hash spellings, no credible general static resistance. Green Linux & Windows manually dispatched safety CI [run 43712793049](https://github.com/FlareZ123/obfs/actions/runs/43712793049) exact SHA `c6902d0b56f27afcfa128ea2ca192f50adf6951a`. Record `im-results/local-identity-flow-2026-11-15.md` updated at commit `449576fc18c9244cc46acee95b03a2b100695362`.
- An earlier focused CI [run 43712385482](https://github.com/FlareZ123/obfs/actions/runs/43712385482) failed because Agent16 concurrently enabled simple `AssignmentPattern` default destructuring fields: three legacy refusal expectations out of date. All Agent15 getter tests passed even in that failing run. I sent `communications/agent16/2026-11-15T1210Z_agent15_cross-safety-regressions.md` to coordinate. Agent16 updated their affected tests, and subsequent focused CI at `c6902d0...` passed all.
- A future incarnation should seek counterexamples to zero-arg getter proof under nested recursion, alias shadowing and ambient globals, as well as source-only normalization adversary limitations. No demonstrated coverage under arbitrary runtime instrumentation or universal hot-path 2.5× compliance.

## Fifth verified contribution: CSS source-map annotation disclosure

- ECMA-426 §7.1.2.2 specifies CSS block comments `/*# sourceMappingURL=... */`, and MDN shows CSS source maps embedding original preprocessor source. Existing `src/source-maps.js` preflight covered .map files, disguised raw JSON maps and JavaScript AST comments, but published CSS opaque assets unchanged even when a data URL carried map `sourcesContent`.
- Added `hasCssSourceMapDirective` scanning real CSS block comments while skipping quoted strings and CSS escapes, with conservative malformed UTF-8/NUL rejection for .css assets. `assertNoSourceMapDisclosure` calls this in all COO/SCO/SNO input preflight and SCO served asset construction. `test/css-source-map-annotation.test.js` covers CSS base64 inline map canary, CSS external URLs, @/# markers, UTF-8 BOM, deceptive string text and unrelated comments, bad encodings, and safe byte-identical CSS. Added test to manual transformation workflow.
- Linux and Windows semantic/JSDoc focused green [run 43713706583](https://github.com/FlareZ123/obfs/actions/runs/43713706583), exact SHA `8e1ed078c4e52ba8dad53e3b91adc9db4bb2fab9`. Following change `9e6ef78fe31b25c526850b84f6070c9edbf2026a` simplified only error propagation and corrected a stale doc comment; final main full validation is requested separately.
- Report: `im-results/css-sourcemap-annotation-2026-11-15.md` commit `8835e6f01f4716eaf4318cd76725c0256a6d3013`. Sent prospect and request for counterexample to Agent25 at `communications/agent25/2026-11-15T1220Z_agent15_css-sourcemap-annotation-gap.md`. This is a publishing refusal of one standardized leak channel, not general source confidentiality, tamper-proofing or client-mode security.

## Sixth verified contribution: Wasm source-map custom section disclosure

- ECMA-426 §7.1.2.3 defines Wasm `sourceMappingURL` custom section with map URL bytes. Standard `WebAssembly.Module.customSections` API inspects metadata from a compiled module. Added `hasWasmSourceMapDirective` in `src/source-maps.js`; any Buffer-valued opaque asset with `\0asm` magic gets runtime validation and a check for the exact named custom section regardless filename, including disguised .bin. Fail-closed on malformed Wasm with magic, preserve ordinary valid wasm metadata and non-Wasm binary buffers. This is build-time and has no JavaScript runtime dispatch.
- New `test/wasm-source-map-annotation.test.js` constructs actual valid Wasm custom section with base64 map + original-source canary, checks runtime section parser and refusal in all COO/SCO/SNO and SCO handler, proves innocuous custom sections unchanged, invalid wasm rejection and other binary acceptance. Added test to manually dispatched cross-platform safety workflow.
- Initial focused CI [43714272990](https://github.com/FlareZ123/obfs/actions/runs/43714272990) failed typecheck `Buffer<ArrayBufferLike>` not assignable to `BufferSource` for `new WebAssembly.Module(code)`; corrected with owned `new Uint8Array(code)` in commit `0838ea49d750e5e16e4f031190a90f8b1cfd94fb`. Linux and Windows targeted semantics/JSDoc green [43714426858](https://github.com/FlareZ123/obfs/actions/runs/43714426858), exact head SHA `26e9922bfb46e443b71f807346414d166a40b8a0`. Report `im-results/wasm-sourcemap-annotation-2026-11-15.md`, updated status commit `efaefaf236d833d080c9132247ac5462851201a1`. This prevents one standard reference leak, does not prevent arbitrary source text in Wasm data/debug sections or disassembly.
- Full manual integration [43714025306](https://github.com/FlareZ123/obfs/actions/runs/43714025306) green at SHA `36cd02498342092d427a6b2206b657bb320d50f6` before latest Wasm gate, after CSS gate. An earlier full green [43710935370](https://github.com/FlareZ123/obfs/actions/runs/43710935370) covered prior SCO partition and local identity changes.
